chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee' said:

A man asked Al-Rida (peace be upon him), and I was listening, about a man who marries a woman for temporary marriage (mut'ah) and stipulates upon her that he will not acknowledge her child, so she brings forth a child afterwards and he denies the child. He (peace be upon him) emphasized this and said, 'He denies, and how can he deny?' out of reverence for it.
The man said, 'And if he accuses her?' He said, 'It is not fitting for you to marry except a trustworthy one.'
Indeed, Allah says: 'The fornicator does not marry except a fornicatress or polytheess, and none marries her except a fornicator or polytheist, and this has been forbidden to the believers.'

key_terms.اَلرِّضَا: Al-Rida (peace be upon him), referring to Imam Ali al-Rida

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man denying a child born from a temporary marriage (mut'ah) if he stipulated non-acknowledgment?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that in temporary marriage (mut'ah), a stipulation to disown a child is invalid because the father cannot simply deny paternity, emphasizing the sanctity of lineage. He links this to Surah An-Nur 24:3, noting that the prohibition on fornicators marrying 'pure' women implies a need for trustworthiness (amanah) in marital relations, ensuring the man is reliable in acknowledging offspring rather than treating the union as purely transactional.
